description:
Clicks, impressions, CTR and average position from Google Search, grouped by any combination of dimensions. This is the whole of the Performance report, as an API.

Give a date range as either period ("last28days") or start_date and end_date. Data is finalised 2–3 days behind, and only the last 16 months are retained.

Two things about the numbers. Rows are capped at row_limit (default 100, maximum 25,000) and paged with start_row. And with the query dimension, Google withholds rare queries for anonymity, so the rows never sum to the property total — query without it when you need a true total.

aggregation_type.description: How impressions are counted. AUTO (default) is right almost always.

data_state.description: FINAL (default) omits the incomplete recent days; ALL includes them; HOURLY_ALL is required for the "hour" dimension.

dimensions.description: Group by these, in this order. Omit for a single totals row. "hour" needs data_state="HOURLY_ALL" and only covers about the last ten days.

end_date.description: Last day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

filter_type.description: How the filters combine. Defaults to "and".

filters.description: Restrict the rows. You do not have to group by a dimension to filter on it. Combined with filter_type.

expression.description: The value to match. Comparisons are case-insensitive. COUNTRY takes a three-letter code such as "deu"; regex operators take RE2 syntax.

period.description: A relative range, resolved against today in Pacific Time — which is the time zone Search Console counts days in. Alternative to start_date/end_date, not combinable with them.

row_limit.description: Rows to return, 100 by default. Raising this is the fastest way to fill a context window with near-identical rows; page with start_row instead where you can.

site_url.description: The Search Console property: "sc-domain:example.com" for a domain property, or "https://example.com/" for a URL-prefix property (the trailing slash is required)

start_date.description: First day of the range, inclusive (YYYY-MM-DD)

start_row.description: Zero-based offset for paging. Defaults to 0.

type.description: Which search surface. Defaults to WEB.

name: query_search_analytics

rowCount.description: How many rows Google returned, shown or not.

rows.description: keys[] plus clicks, impressions, ctr and position — the rows the table shows, which is every row unless truncated says otherwise.

truncated.description: Present only when entries were dropped to fit the budget.

title: Query search analytics
